datasets.name: basic_simulation
datasets.description: A standard page reference string for basic FIFO, LRU, and Optimal simulation. Contains a mix of repeated and new pages to demonstrate both hits and faults.

datasets.name: page_hit_heavy
datasets.description: A sequence with many repeated pages that fit within the frame count, resulting in a high hit ratio for all algorithms.
datasets.purpose: Demonstrate high hit ratio when pages fit in memory

datasets.name: page_fault_heavy
datasets.description: A sequence where every page is unique and exceeds the frame count, causing a fault on every access.
datasets.purpose: Demonstrate worst-case scenario with 100% page faults

datasets.name: replacement_demonstration
datasets.description: Designed to show different replacement decisions across FIFO, LRU, and Optimal. After frames fill, the algorithms diverge in which page they evict.
datasets.purpose: Highlight how replacement strategy affects which page is evicted

datasets.name: algorithm_comparison
datasets.description: A longer sequence specifically crafted to produce different fault counts across FIFO, LRU, and Optimal, making algorithm comparison meaningful.
datasets.purpose: Compare all three algorithms on a dataset where their results differ

datasets.name: single_page
datasets.description: A trivial sequence containing only one repeated page. All accesses after the first should be hits regardless of algorithm.

datasets.name: single_frame
datasets.description: Only one memory frame is available. Every page change causes a fault. Tests minimum-frame behavior.

datasets.name: frames_exceed_pages
datasets.description: More frames than unique pages. After all unique pages are loaded, every subsequent access is a hit.
datasets.purpose: Edge case: more frames than unique pages means no replacement needed
